t: Welcome to Pudding Lane, a small street in the City of London running between Eastcheap and Thames Street. This is where Thomas Farriner's bakery stood, and it's where the Great Fire of London began in 1666. It crosses Monument Street, where Christopher Wren's Monument to the Great Fire stands. William Ingram, who lived from 1639 to 1706 and wrote to the Quaker Phineas Pemberton in the 1680s, lived here, so he was a resident of this lane in the years before and after those events.
